official_title.value: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Nemolizumab in Subjects With Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis With Inadequate Response to or for Whom Cyclosporine A is Not Medically Advisable

why_stopped.value: The study data will not be utilized in the IND and is only being conducted in EU.

value.description: Participants will receive loading dose of 60 milligram (2×30 mg) subcutaneous (SC) injection of nemolizumab at baseline. Thereafter 30 mg nemolizumab will be administered via single SC injection once in 4 week (Q4W) up to week 12.
Participants will receive loading dose of 60 mg (2×30 mg) SC injection of placebo at baseline. Thereafter 30 mg placebo will be administered via single SC injection Q4W up to week 12.

dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule.interventions: Nemolizumab and CD14152 placebo dose descriptions: "Nemolizumab" "Participants will receive loading dose of 60 milligram (2×30 mg) subcutaneous (SC) injection of nemolizumab at baseline." "Thereafter 30 mg nemolizumab will be administered via single SC injection once in 4 week (Q4W) up to week 12." "Nemolizumab" "CD14152 placebo" "Participants will receive loading dose of 60 mg (2×30 mg) SC injection of placebo at baseline." "Thereafter 30 mg placebo will be administered via single SC injection Q4W up to week 12." "Placebo" -- The typed dose_value represents the recurring 30 mg dose; the registry separately specifies a 60 mg (2×30 mg) loading dose at baseline. Both interventions are administered by single subcutaneous injection Q4W through week 12. No administration site or antibody details are provided in these descriptions.

severity_criteria.source_excerpt: protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria: Inclusion criteria 2–4: "A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Nemolizumab in Subjects With Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis With Inadequate Response to or for Whom Cyclosporine A is Not Medically Advisable" "2." "EASI score ≥ 20 at both the screening and baseline visits." "Participant with an EASI score of 18-19 at the screening visit only may be reevaluated once within 48 hours." "3." "IGA score ≥ 3 (based on the IGA scale ranging from 0 to 4, in which 3 is moderate and 4 is severe) at both the screening and baseline visits." "4." "AD involvement ≥ 10% of BSA at both the screening and baseline visits." "The EASI score can range from 0 to 72 with higher scores representing greater severity of atopic dermatitis." -- EASI, IGA, and BSA thresholds apply at both screening and baseline. IGA anchors are taken directly from the eligibility text; criterion 2 permits reevaluation only for EASI 18–19 at screening.

value.background_agent_class: topical corticosteroids (TCS), with or without topical calcineurin inhibitors (TCI)
permitted_concomitant: Authorized TCS, with or without TCI, as determined appropriate by the investigator
value.population_note: Adults with moderate-to-severe AD inadequately controlled with or not advised to use oral CsA for medical reasons.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: protocolSection.descriptionModule.briefSummary and eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria inclusion criterion 6: "Efficacy and Safety of Nemolizumab in Subjects With Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis With Inadequate Response to or for Whom Cyclosporine A is Not Medically Advisable" "The primary objective of this study is to investigate the efficacy of nemolizumab administered in combination with topical background therapy (topical corticosteroids \[TCS\] with or without topical calcineurin inhibitors \[TCI\]) in adult participants with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD) who are not adequately controlled with or are not advised to use oral cyclosporine A (CsA) for medical reasons." "The secondary objective is to investigate the safety of nemolizumab in adult participants with moderate-to-severe AD who are not adequately controlled with or are not advised to use oral CsA for medical reasons." "6." "Agree to apply a moisturizer throughout the study from the screening visit; agree to apply an authorized TCS, with or without TCI, from the screening visit and throughout the study as determined appropriate by the investigator." -- The summary explicitly describes nemolizumab in combination with topical background therapy; eligibility specifies moisturizer and authorized TCS with or without TCI throughout the study. The registry text reviewed does not specify a TCS regimen or a during-treatment prohibited-concomitant list; an empty prohibited list means no specific prohibited agent is represented here, not that all concomitant therapy is allowed. The CsA medical-advisability wording describes the target population, not a treatment-period prohibition.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule.interventions and outcomesModule.primaryOutcomes: "Thereafter 30 mg nemolizumab will be administered via single SC injection once in 4 week (Q4W) up to week 12." "Thereafter 30 mg placebo will be administered via single SC injection Q4W up to week 12." "Proportion of Participants with Eczema Area and Severity Index-75 (EASI-75) (≥ 75% Improvement in EASI from Baseline) at Week 16" "Week 16" "Proportion of Participants with an Improvement of Peak Pruritus Numeric Rating Scale (PP NRS) ≥ 4 at Week 16" "Week 16" "Incidence and Severity of Adverse Events (AEs), Including Adverse Events of Special Interest (AESIs), Treatment Emergent AEs (TEAEs), and serious AEs (SAEs)" "Baseline through week 24" -- The two registered intervention descriptions state Q4W dosing through Week 12; this supports last_injection_week=12, not an end of treatment period. Both primary outcome time frames state Week 16. The safety outcome is followed through Week 24, but that assessment horizon does not establish an end-of-study week or the intervening period boundaries. The cited CT.gov file is registry narrative, with no full per-visit schedule table; visit weeks and cadence are therefore not populated from outcome time frames.
